clue.text: Insect filling type of chocolate banana

indicators.note: one thing filling another sits inside it, so the insect goes into the chocolate

parts.note: plain chocolate is dark chocolate without milk
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug is found inside a chocolate-coated banana.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a large starchy cooking variety of banana.

clue.text: French try to stand up one they've made legless?

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A Frenchman attempts to get to his feet after drinking himself legless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' looks like British slang for very drunk, but the definition plays on the French reputation for eating frogs' legs, which leaves the frog legless.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs' legs are a French delicacy, so the French are cheekily said to leave the frog without its legs.

clue.text: Watch, entering black wood

indicators.note: the black letter goes into the word for a watch, entering it

parts.note: a timer is a device that watches the time
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A watch slipping into a black wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber is wood prepared or grown for building.

clue.text: Dead end — my crosswords aren't innovative

parts.note: the setter speaking of his own crosswords stands for himself, I am, contracted
work that is no longer innovative is passé, out of date

explanation.surface: The setter despairs that his puzzles have reached a dead end of originality.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as the setter talking: if his crosswords are stale, then he is passé, 'I'm passé'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation with no way forward, a deadlock or blind alley.

clue.text: Kindly interest shown when oil and gold distributed about a quarter

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the compass point
the letters are spread around in a new order

parts.note: W, west, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Benevolence displayed when oil and gold are shared around a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges the oil and gold letters, and 'about' wraps the result round the compass quarter, splitting it into good + ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is friendly, kindly feeling or interest towards others.

clue.text: Grilled dish infant king brought up, mum having doctored his first

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means be quiet: sh

indicators.note: something doctored has been tampered with, so the letters are altered
in a down entry, brought up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a babe is an infant
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A baby prince is raised by his mother, who has tampered with his food first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctored' rearranges HIS, which follows the mum piece; 'first' says that part leads, before 'brought up' reverses infant plus king.
explanation.definitionFit: Shish kebab is meat cubes grilled on a skewer.

clue.text: Waste comic picture frames?

indicators.note: one word frames another by surrounding it like a picture frame

parts.note: to picture something is to see it in the mind
a wag is a joker, a comic

explanation.surface: Asking whether a comic picture is worth framing or simply rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste matter carried off in sewers.

clue.text: Consideration for others, a platitude by the left

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a truism is a trite, self-evident statement

explanation.surface: Being kind to others dismissed as a left-wing cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless concern for the welfare of others.

clue.text: Natural earth's core hot, terribly

indicators.note: done terribly, the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Geology: the centre of the planet is ferociously hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy natural pigment of iron oxide and clay.

clue.text: Pub room where those with barrels rolling

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word round, back to front

parts.note: guns have barrels

explanation.surface: A bar where beer barrels are rolled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrels' suggests beer in the pub; here they are gun barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug is a small cosy private room in a British pub.

clue.text: Bishop offered alternative to strip poker? That's sweet

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess
a randy snap would be a lustful version of the card game snap, a substitute for strip poker

explanation.surface: A clergyman proposing a racy card game finds it rather nice.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap is a simple card game; 'randy' (British for lustful) makes it a saucy rival to strip poker.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp rolled ginger biscuit, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Figaro composer

definitions.meaning: Figaro is the title character of Rossini's opera about a Seville hairdresser
Samuel ... was the American composer of the Adagio for Strings

explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the Barber of Seville, and Samuel Barber was a twentieth-century American composer.

clue.text: Home builder finds good egg with hen

parts.note: a brick is old slang for a reliable good sort
a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: A builder discovers a decent egg alongside a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer is a tradesman who builds houses from bricks.

clue.text: One noting details finds shilling on Ken Dodd?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
the British comedian Ken Dodd was famous for waving a feather duster he called his tickling stick, making him a tickler

explanation.surface: A pedant finds a shilling on a well-known comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on attention to precise details.

clue.text: Exit in a tizzy amid a bit of concern

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit amid the other word

parts.note: any means some, a bit of, as in any milk

indicators.note: being in a tizzy is being in a flustered state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Leaving in a fluster shows some worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tizzy' jumbles EXIT into XIET, put amid ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety is worry or concern about what may happen.

clue.text: Court has its process around Chelsea, perhaps

indicators.note: the court's process goes around the other piece

parts.note: a court's process is a trial
a Chelsea bun is a sticky spiral currant bun

explanation.surface: A court case concerning the London district of Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea seems to be the London area or football club; it is a type of bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a court or body set up to judge disputes.

clue.text: A state? By degrees it is

parts.note: the French a la means in the manner of, by way of
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Asking whether a nation is reached gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' looks like 'gradually' but splits into a la (French for in the style of) and two university degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the southern United States.

clue.text: Same old thing, New Labour's one man band?

parts.note: mono is a prefix meaning one
Tony Blair was the leader of New Labour

explanation.surface: Mocking New Labour as a single-man band.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-man band of Tony Blair would be a mono-Tony: the joke behind 'man band?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is tedious sameness, the same thing over and over.

clue.text: Smell appears strong during drink, in by-product of drinking

indicators.note: the drink piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pee, urine, is what drinking ultimately produces

indicators.note: the strong piece comes during the drink, inside it

parts.note: rum is a drink
F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong

explanation.surface: A strong odour turns up while drinking, a side effect of boozing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'during' puts the strong letter in the drink, and 'in' puts that inside the by-product of drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfume is a pleasant smell or scent.

clue.text: Second team behind

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A reserve team sits at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside is an informal word for the behind, the buttocks.

clue.text: Powerful woman a bloke weightlifting's impressed

indicators.note: pressed into another word, the piece goes inside it

parts.note: a bloke is a man
read as weight lifting: oz, an ounce, is a weight, and lifted up in a down entry it reads zo

explanation.surface: A strong woman is impressed by a man lifting weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weightlifting' looks like the bloke's sport but splits into weight + lifting, a reversed ounce; 'impressed' presses that into A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amazon, from the legendary female warriors, is a tall strong woman.

clue.text: Pipes to discard in small vessel

indicators.note: the discard piece sits in the vessel

parts.note: a tug is a small boat
to bin something is to throw it out

explanation.surface: Instructions to dispose of pipes in a little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubing is lengths of tube, pipes collectively.

clue.text: Residence where support keeps ladder up

indicators.note: a thing that keeps another holds it safe inside, so the support goes round the ladder piece

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: A building where a support holds a ladder upright.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is British for a run in tights; 'up' turns that word round in this down entry, and 'keeps' sets it inside the golf support.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is occupancy of a property, residence by right.

clue.text: King — one cooks cake for guttersnipe

parts.note: R is rex, Latin for king
an Aga is a large British cast-iron range cooker
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A monarch's chef bakes a little cake for a street urchin.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy range cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a ragged dirty child, a guttersnipe.

clue.text: Destiny of subdominant and leading note

parts.note: in tonic sol-fa, fa is the fourth note of the scale, the subdominant
te, the seventh note, is the leading note that leads up to the tonic

explanation.surface: A musical question: the destiny of two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is destiny, what is bound to happen.

clue.text: Pacific republic providing uprising — jail regularly follows

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising up means reading upwards

parts.note: if means providing, on condition that

indicators.note: taking letters regularly picks every other one

explanation.surface: A revolt in a Pacific state is followed by routine imprisonment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' just places the jail letters after FI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is an island republic in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Sophocles' last mantra takes time receding

parts.note: om is a sacred mantra

indicators.note: going back, so read backwards

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The Greek playwright's final chant takes a long time to fade.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophocles wrote in Greek, whose last letter is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, the one Sophocles would end with.

clue.text: Name given to cannabis "horse" about a month after unknown

indicators.note: the horse goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: after sends the month second, behind the unknown letter

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
Jan is short for January

explanation.surface: Cannabis is dubbed horse, roughly a month after it appears from nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is also slang for heroin, a drug red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Jane is a slang name for marijuana.
